summary: N. D. Mironov was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Leipzig University (~1902–1903) and under Hermann Jacobi (~1903–1905) and Heinrich Hübschmann (~1904–1906).

N. S. Ramanuja Tatacharya worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as Vice Chancellor of National Sanskrit University (1989–1994) and as a researcher at the French Institute of Pondicherry (~1989–2017).

Indologist N. Veezhinathan earned his PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University (-1964) under A. Sankaran and studied under T. S. Srinivasa Sastri. He was a research scholar at Deccan College (1960–1963) and became Lecturer in Sanskrit at University of Madras (1964).

N. Venkataramanayya worked in Indology, history, and archaeology after studying under Ferrand E. Corley. He served as Reader of Indian History and Archæology at the University of Madras and as Deputy Director for Epigraphy in Andhra Pradesh's Department of Archaeology and Museums.

Nae Ionescu worked in philosophy and religious studies, studying at the University of Bucharest (~1908–1912), University of Göttingen (~1912–1913), and University of Munich (~1913–1919). He later held a post at the University of Bucharest (~1919–1938).
Nagin J. Shah is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who succeeded Dalsukh D. Malvania and served as Acting Director of the Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Institute of Indology (attested 1968).

Nalinaksha Dutt was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned degrees from Calcutta, London, and SOAS, studying under Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He headed Calcutta's Pali department (~1939–1958) and presided over The Asiatic Society (1959–1961).

Nalini Balbir specializes in Indology and linguistics. After studying under Colette Caillat (~1975–1980), she held posts at CNRS (1982–1988), Sorbonne Nouvelle University (1988), INALCO (~1988), and École Pratique des Hautes Études (2000).
Nalini Devdas works in religious studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Concordia University under Leslie Orr (attested 2004) and held a post at Carleton University (attested 2004).

Nam-lin Hur specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Princeton University (PhD under Helen Hardacre), completed a Harvard postdoctoral fellowship, and became professor of Japanese history and religious culture at UBC.

Naman P. Ahuja is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his doctorate at SOAS University of London and serves as Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2018).

Namgyal Rinpoche was a Buddhist and religious studies teacher who studied at Jarvis Baptist Seminary, University of Michigan, and under traditional teachers including Mahasi Sayadaw and the 16th Karmapa. He founded Kagyu Samye Ling (1965) and the Dharma Centre of Canada (1966).

Namio Egami was an archaeology, history, and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930). He held a post there (~1948–1967) and served as Director of the Ancient Orient Museum (~1978–2002).
Namita Das is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who completed her PhD at Gauhati University under the doctoral supervision of Sibnath Sarma (attested 2012).

Namkhai Norbu was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Derge Gonchen, Kuse Serjong Shedra, and under Changchub Dorje. He held posts at ISMEO (~1960–1964) and University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1962–1992), and founded the Shang Shung Institute (1990).

Nancy Hock is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley (-1987) under Joanna Gottfried Williams and held a post at the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco (attested 1987).
Nancy Lin is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who pursued graduate study at Columbia University and earned her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley.

Nancy McCagney works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, Gerald James Larson, William F. Powell, and Andrew Rawlinson, and held a post at the University of Delaware (attested 1997).

Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She has held posts as a Project Fellow at Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (attested 2011) and as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Historical Research.
Nang Dzé Drubpé Dorjé studied under Shechen Gyaltsab and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
